tools.name: move_task_to_sprint_and_reassign
tools.description: Moves a task from its current sprint into another sprint and transfers ownership of the task to a new assignee.

params.name: task_id
params.description: ID of the task to move

params.name: target_sprint_id
params.description: ID of the sprint that will receive the task

params.name: new_assignee
params.description: Username of the new task owner

tools.code:
import sqlite3

DB_PATH = "projects.db"

from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("sprints")


@mcp.tool()
def move_task_to_sprint_and_reassign(task_id: int, target_sprint_id: int, new_assignee: str) -> dict:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    try:
        row = conn.execute("SELECT sprint_id, assignee FROM tasks WHERE id = ?", (task_id,)).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return {"success": False, "error": f"Task {task_id} not found"}
        old_sprint, old_assignee = row
        conn.execute(
            "UPDATE tasks SET sprint_id = ?, assignee = ? WHERE id = ?",
            (target_sprint_id, new_assignee, task_id),
        )
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()
    result = {
        "success": True,
        "task_id": task_id,
        "from_sprint": old_sprint,
        "to_sprint": target_sprint_id,
        "previous_assignee": old_assignee,
        "new_assignee": new_assignee,
    }
    return result

tools.name: post_sprint_summary_to_slack
tools.description: Records a sprint's status as closed-out-reviewed in the database and posts a summary of its completed and open tasks to the team's Slack webhook.

params.name: sprint_id
params.description: ID of the sprint to summarize

params.name: webhook_url
params.description: Slack incoming webhook URL to post to

tools.code:
import sqlite3
import requests

from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("sprints")

DB_PATH = "projects.db"


def _build_summary(conn, sprint_id):
    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM tasks WHERE sprint_id = ? GROUP BY status",
        (sprint_id,),
    ).fetchall()
    counts = {status: n for status, n in rows}
    done = counts.get("done", 0)
    open_count = sum(n for s, n in counts.items() if s != "done")
    return f"Sprint {sprint_id}: {done} tasks done, {open_count} still open"


@mcp.tool()
def post_sprint_summary_to_slack(sprint_id: int, webhook_url: str) -> str:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    try:
        text = _build_summary(conn, sprint_id)
        conn.execute("UPDATE sprints SET review_status = 'reviewed' WHERE id = ?", (sprint_id,))
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()
    resp = requests.post(webhook_url, json={"text": text}, timeout=10)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return text

tools.name: transfer_backlog_items_to_sprint
tools.description: Looks up a project owner's backlog items, moves them into a sprint, and makes the sprint's lead the new owner of those items. Returns the items that were moved.

params.name: project_id
params.description: ID of the project whose backlog is read

params.name: sprint_id
params.description: ID of the sprint receiving the items

params.name: sprint_lead
params.description: Username of the sprint lead who becomes owner

tools.code:
import sqlite3
from contextlib import closing

from agents import function_tool as tool

DB_PATH = "projects.db"


@tool
def transfer_backlog_items_to_sprint(project_id: int, sprint_id: int, sprint_lead: str) -> list:
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)) as conn:
        with conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                "SELECT id, title FROM tasks WHERE project_id = ? AND sprint_id IS NULL",
                (project_id,),
            ).fetchall()
            ids = [r[0] for r in rows]
            for task_id in ids:
                conn.execute(
                    "UPDATE tasks SET sprint_id = ?, owner = ? WHERE id = ?",
                    (sprint_id, sprint_lead, task_id),
                )
    return [{"id": r[0], "title": r[1]} for r in rows]
